title: Finance: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, RevRec & Billing Guidance (Q2 2024)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This guidance consolidates Redwood Inference's operating practices for annual and quarterly budgeting and forecasting, procurement and purchasing workflows, contract lifecycle handoffs, and the high-level revenue recognition and billing policy principles used by Finance and Legal. The goal is to provide a single, practical reference for owners and reviewers to ensure consistent approvals, clear handoffs, and compliant accounting treatment.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood entities for corporate operating expenses, capital requests, third-party contracts, and customer billing setups.
- Exceptions must be escalated to VP Finance with Legal review.

Contents:
1) Budgeting and Forecasting (owner: FP&A)
   Overview:
   - Annual budget is prepared on a fiscal-year basis; rolling quarterly forecasts (12 months) are maintained with monthly updates during close.
   - Primary objectives: align headcount and cloud/GPU spend to product roadmap, plan Dedicated and Private capacity commitments, and quantify cash requirements for reserved capacity contracts.

   Calendar and milestones (example):
   1. Budget kickoff: mid-June
   2. Department submissions due: July 31
   3. Executive review & iteration: August
   4. Final board budget approval: Sept 15
   5. First forecast refresh: end of Q3

   Inputs and owners:
   - Headcount plan: People Ops (owner: People Ops lead for each org)
   - Infrastructure & reserved capacity estimates: Eng Infra (owner: Head of Infra)
more_content:
- Revenue and bookings: Sales & RevOps (owner: Head of RevOps)
   - Product roadmaps and launches: Product (owner: Product Leads)

   Forecasting best practices:
   - Use centralized FP&A model (Google Sheets / BigQuery source-of-truth) with per-department tabs and change logs.
   - Annotate major assumptions (e.g., model unit costs, expected Dedicated deals) and publish a one-page sensitivity analysis for +/-10% GPU cost variance.

   Approval thresholds & signoffs:
   - Department-level variances >10% from plan require reforecast and executive review.
   - Any incremental committed spend for Dedicated/Private capacity >$250k ARR requires VP Finance and Head of Eng approval.

2) Procurement & Purchasing (owner: Finance - Procurement)
   Purpose:
   - Ensure controls over third-party spend, consistent vendor onboarding, and clear approval flows for one-time and committed purchases.

   Procurement tiers and approval matrix:
   - Tier 1: <= $5k - Department Head approval (submit PO request in Coupa)
   - Tier 2: > $5k and <= $50k - Department Head + Finance Manager approval
   - Tier 3: > $50k and <= $250k - Department Head + Finance Director approval + Procurement review
   - Tier 4: > $250k - VP Finance approval + Legal review (contract required)

   Process (step-by-step):
   1. Requestor creates procurement request in Coupa with cost center, GL code, invoice contact, and supporting quote(s).
   2. Finance/Procurement reviews vendor (sanctions screening, W9/W8 collection for US entities).
   3. If contract required, Legal is looped for redlines and final sign-off (see Contracts section).
   4. Once approved, Procurement issues PO and logs committed spend in the procurement tracker.
   5. Accounts Payable processes invoices to PO against receipt.

   Vendor onboarding checklist:
   - Business name & tax ID
   - Primary contact, billing contact, and bank details
   - Insurance and SOC2 evidence (if handling customer data or infrastructure)
   - Payment terms (Net 30 default)

   Exceptions & emergency procurement:
   - Emergency purchases (e.g., urgent capacity to meet customer SLA) must be approved by Finance Director and logged within 48 hours; retroactive approvals are discouraged and require an incident justification.

3) Contracts and Legal Process (owner: Legal)
   Objective:
   - Standardize contract lifecycle from request to signature and archive, with clear responsibilities between Sales, Legal, Finance, and Product.

   Contract types covered:
   - Customer master services agreements (MSAs), SOWs, Dedicated capacity contracts, partner and vendor agreements, NDAs.

   Lifecycle & responsibilities:
   1. Contract request: Sales / Procurement submits contract request via Salesforce/Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system with template selection.
   2. Legal intake: Legal triages, assigns a contract owner, and identifies required attachments (SLA, security addendum, pricing schedules).
   3. Negotiation: Sales owns commercial negotiation; Legal performs legal risk review and redlines.
   4. Signature: Approval matrix applied - commercial terms approved by Sales Manager; any nonstandard indemnity, data residency, or liability caps >$500k require Legal Director + VP Finance sign-off.
   5. Execution & storage: Fully executed contracts uploaded to CLM and indexed with metadata (customer name, contract type, start/end dates, renewal terms, revenue recognition attributes).

   Key legal controls and red flags:
   - No customer contractual commitment for running Protected Customer Data in non-compliant regions without Security sign-off.
   - Liability caps: default to fees paid in 12 months; deviations require Legal Director approval.
   - Auto-renewal: flagged and requires Customer Success review 90 days before renewal.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies (owner: RevRec / Accounting)
   Principles (alignment with ASC 606 / IFRS 15):
   - Revenue recognized when the company satisfies performance obligations and has a contract with enforceable rights.
   - Distinguish between billed amounts (cash/AR) and recognized revenue (GAAP).

   Typical product revenue patterns at Redwood:
   - Hosted API usage: usage-based revenue recognized as services are delivered (over the billing period).
   - Dedicated capacity: for committed-capacity contracts with upfront prepayments, revenue is recognized over the contracted service period; for nonrefundable upfront fees that represent distinct services, allocate per performance obligation.
   - Private/on-prem licensing: recognize perpetually if license is distinct and right to use is granted; professional services (onboarding) recognized over time as performed.

   Billing cadence and invoicing:
   - Usage invoices: monthly in arrears with detailed token/embedding usage lines.
   - Reserved capacity: invoiced per contract terms (monthly/quarterly/annual).
   - One-time fees (e.g., setup, migration): invoiced per SOW milestones or on execution, recognition follows GAAP allocation.

   Revenue recognition workflow (high level):
   1. Contract metadata captured in CLM (including performance obligations, billing schedule, contract start/end, and variable consideration caps).
   2. RevRec team reviews monthly billing exports and maps billed amounts to recognized revenue in the accounting system.
   3. Any complex arrangements (multi-element, significant variable consideration, refunds/credits) are escalated to Head of Accounting for judgment and disclosure.

   Internal controls and thresholds:
   - Material contract adjustments (> $250k impact) require CFO approval and disclosure in monthly close notes.
   - Credits/Refunds > $50k require Finance Director and Customer Success sign-off.

   Billing disputes and collections:
   - Dispute intake: Customer Success opens ticket with billing_support tag and includes disputed invoice lines and supporting logs.
   - Collections: AR aging triggers collections workflow at 30/60/90 days. 90+ day delinquent accounts are escalated to Sales leadership and Legal for potential collections or hold on services.

Appendices and templates:
- Procurement request template (fields required): requestor, cost center, GL code, business justification, vendor quote URL, contract required (Y/N), expected delivery date.
- Contract intake checklist: customer name, sales rep, contract type, payment terms, SLA requirements, data residency clause, renewal notification window.
- RevRec mapping table (example lines):
   Product Type | Billing Method | Revenue Recognition
   Hosted API | Monthly arrears | Recognize as used (monthly)
   Dedicated reserved | Prepaid annual | Recognize ratably over term
   On-prem license | One-time perpetual | Recognize on delivery when distinct

Review cadence:

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: How do we treat refundable onboarding credits?
A: Refundable credits are treated as variable consideration and recognized when probable and estimable; until then they reduce recognized revenue when applied.

Q: Who approves purchasing a new GPU supplier with committed capacity?
A: Procurement + Finance Director for tier 3, VP Finance and Legal for >$250k.

Q: Where are contracts stored?
A: All executed contracts must be uploaded to the CLM with the contract owner metadata populated.
